name: Object Pascal
_comment: Object Pascal (Delphi 13) TextMate grammar for the drag-lint extension.
TWO RULES GOVERN THIS FILE.
1. ORDER: the compiler-directive patterns MUST be tried before the comment
patterns. '{ ... }' is a comment but '{$...}' is a directive, and they
must not share a scope -- colouring {$IFDEF} as a comment is wrong, and
this repo has hit the same confusion at the parser level (a nested '}'
inside a brace comment ended it early and cost a build). The comment
rules additionally guard with a negative lookahead so the ordering is
not the ONLY thing holding it up.
2. SUFFIX: every scope ends in '.pascal'. That is load-bearing. The
'Apply RAD Studio Colours' command writes editor.tokenColorCustomizations
globally, and the .pascal suffix is the only thing confining those rules
to Pascal files instead of recolouring every language the user opens.
run_pascal_grammar_and_theme.ps1 fails on a scope without it.
Known and accepted: a TextMate grammar is a regex cascade with no parser
behind it, so it disagrees with our tree-sitter parse in the corners --
generics vs comparison (AreEqual<Integer> vs A < B), nested {$IFDEF}
regions, asm bodies. That is inherent to the mechanism. The fix is
textDocument/semanticTokens fed by the real parse, which VS Code layers OVER
this grammar; it is a complement, not a replacement.

patterns.name: keyword.control.directive.pascal
patterns._comment: {$IFDEF} / {$R *.dfm} / {$I unit.inc}. Ends at the first '}' -- Delphi brace comments and directives do not nest.

patterns.name: comment.line.double-slash.pascal
patterns._comment: Covers '///' DocInsight comments too: the IDE draws them with the same Comment element, and fidelity to the IDE beats inventing a distinction it does not make.

patterns.name: string.quoted.single.pascal
patterns._comment: Delphi 12+ multi-line string. The opening ''' must be last on its line, which is what keeps this from swallowing the '''' that writes one quote character.

patterns.name: constant.character.escape.pascal
patterns._comment: Delphi escapes a quote by doubling it -- 'It''s'. There are no backslash escapes.

patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.pascal
patterns._comment: Digits are REQUIRED after the dot so the subrange '1..5' does not read as the float '1.'.
storage.type.pascal, matching the #keywords list: this rule runs first, so scoping 'procedure' differently here would give the same word two scopes depending on whether a name followed it.
